summary: 金管會與環境部今天（9/23）共同宣布調整上市櫃公司接軌IFRS永續揭露準則的相關規定，在國家永續目標不變的前提下，參考歐盟及亞洲近期簡化永續揭露要求的趨勢，改採較符合企業準備程度的分層推動方式。此次的調整，強制適用IFRS永續揭露準則的上市櫃公司，將由原規劃約1,970家縮減至約560家，主要鎖定實收資本額20億元以上，以及受環境部納管、需進行溫室氣體盤查及查驗的企業。 金管會表示，雖然強制適用的家數降低，但納入企業的市值仍占全體上市櫃公司逾87%，涵蓋資本市場主要企業。這次調整並非降低永續揭露要求，而是重新安排接軌順序，先協助大型企業建立符合國際準則的永續資訊揭露能力，再逐步推動其他企業提升相關能力。

title: Bowel cancer “melted away” after immunotherapy, then stayed away

title: A surprisingly simple way to relieve knee arthritis pain without pills or surgery
summary: A surprisingly simple change in how you walk could help relieve knee arthritis pain and even slow joint damage. In a year-long clinical trial, researchers found that adjusting the angle of a person's foot while walking reduced osteoarthritis pain by an amount comparable to medication, without requiring drugs or surgery. Even more promising, MRI scans revealed that participants who adopted the personalized walking technique experienced slower deterioration in a marker of knee cartilage health.

title: A plastic once thought harmless may be fueling fatty liver disease
summary: One of the world's most common plastics may pose a hidden threat to liver health. Texas A&M researchers discovered that polyethylene microplastics can contribute to fatty liver disease, with potentially worse effects when combined with an unhealthy diet. Even more surprising, this widely used plastic was previously considered relatively harmless.

title: Eating olive oil before carbs has a surprising effect on blood sugar
summary: A simple change in the order you eat your food could help prevent blood sugar spikes. Scientists discovered that giving mice olive oil before carbohydrates slowed digestion and activated a surprising combination of hormones and nerve signals that helped regulate blood sugar, even in mice with type 2 diabetes.

title: Neanderthals may have used prehistoric glue as an ancient antibiotic
summary: Neanderthals may have used a sticky substance made from birch bark to treat wounds thousands of years before antibiotics existed. Researchers recreated ancient birch tar production techniques and discovered that every sample could inhibit the growth of bacteria responsible for dangerous wound infections. Previously known mainly as a prehistoric glue, birch tar may have doubled as a surprisingly effective natural medicine.

title: A protein that fuels cancer could also be the key to fighting it
summary: Scientists have discovered how to turn a protein that normally fuels cancer growth into a weapon against it. By activating PPARD in immune cells, researchers made them better at burning fat and attacking tumors, slowing or stopping cancer growth in laboratory experiments. The approach showed promise against colorectal, breast, and ovarian cancers, as well as melanoma.

title: USC scientists discover how to create a never-ending supply of cancer-fighting cells
summary: USC scientists have discovered a way to create a potentially renewable supply of genetically engineered immune cells that can attack cancer and strengthen the body's natural defenses. By growing and modifying immature immune cells rather than mature ones, researchers developed a system that can continuously produce tumor-fighting cells inside the body.

title: Scientists discover how exercise reverses muscle aging
summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden biological mechanism that helps explain how exercise can reverse some of the damage caused by muscle aging. The key is a gene called DEAF1, which becomes overactive with age and interferes with the muscles’ ability to clear damaged proteins and repair themselves. Exercise can help restore this balance, allowing older muscles to rebuild and regain strength, although the benefits may diminish when the system becomes too disrupted.

title: Just 3,000 steps a day may help slow Alzheimer's, scientists find
summary: Walking just 3,000 steps a day could help slow Alzheimer’s-related brain changes, according to new research. Scientists discovered that physical activity was linked to less buildup of harmful tau proteins and nearly half the cognitive and functional decline, even in people already showing early signs of the disease. The strongest benefits appeared at 5,000 to 7,500 daily steps, suggesting that the popular 10,000-step goal may not be necessary.
